findings.title: Continuance becomes chosen inaction
findings.claim: The duration clause can make the opponents' continued presence the outer condition against which the speakers fix their own continuing non-action: permanence outside is answered by permanence inside.
findings.mechanism: The focus form دَامُوا carries the registered yerinde kalıp sürmek branch, while the closing قَاعِدُونَ supplies the independent focus act of staying back. The exact 9:83 connection joins permanent refusal to being told to sit, returning that wider behavioral pattern through the focus sitting act.
findings.reader_payoff: The condition is no longer heard as neutral timing alone; it exposes a self-sealing arrangement in which an imagined lasting obstacle becomes a lasting decision not to act.
findings.containment: This is a qualified relation between the focus words and the 9:83 pattern. It does not claim that دَامُوا itself means sitting, that the opponents' presence is metaphysically endless, or that the wider passage is the same historical scene.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is registered and the wider target Arabic is supplied, but the reader-walk support is legacy_unbound and the connection target has no supplied morphology or lexical analysis.

findings.title: Sitting becomes withdrawn agency
findings.claim: The final قَاعِدُونَ names more than a bodily posture: in the face of a demanded advance, the speakers place themselves among those who withdraw from the action while sending the causal task to others.
findings.mechanism: The registered q-d branch is eylemden geri durma, carried by the focus active participle after the speakers delegate fighting to Moses and his Lord. The exact 9:83 passage joins permanent refusal to being told to sit, and 3:168 joins sitting out conflict to counterfactual speech, giving the focus posture a wider social-action contour.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear 'we are sitting here' as an active withdrawal of responsibility, not as an inert location report.
findings.containment: The resonance supports a withdrawal-of-agency reading without proving a single motive, hypocrisy, or identity of narrative circumstances across the cited ayat.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and carrier are registered, while the reader-walk support is legacy_unbound and the exact wider connections supply target Arabic without target morphology.

findings.title: Assigned access becomes self-exclusion
findings.claim: The speakers turn an assigned entry into a self-authored exclusion: their unlimited refusal treats access to the land as unavailable, and the following prohibition echoes that chosen bar back as an imposed condition.
findings.mechanism: The focus دَخُلَ carrier supplies entry and the focus أَبَدًا carrier supplies an unlimited duration. The exact HFT roles place these against 5:1's controlled release vocabulary, 5:21's assigned land, and 5:26's explicit prohibition, changing a refusal of access under enemy presence into a bounded self-ban that is answered by prohibition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the refusal cross from describing an obstacle to constructing a boundary around the speakers themselves, with the later ayah returning that boundary as their lived restriction.
findings.containment: This is a qualified legal-boundary resonance, not a claim that the focus words alone create a legal ruling. The unresolved context branches have no verified glosses or facets, and the alternative remains that the language is strategic refusal without legal coloring.

epistemic.reason: The two focus branches are registered and the HFT context coordinates and Arabic anchors are exact, but the HFT reader is legacy_unbound and three context branches remain lexically unresolved.

findings.title: The go-command changes function

findings.mechanism: The registered ذ ه ب branch is gitme, geçme ve uzaklaşma, carried by the focus imperative. The exact 20:42 and 26:15 connections repeat the go-command with paired agents and signs, then return through the focus pair ٱنتَ وَرَبُّكَ and the dual fight imperative, where the speakers remain seated.
findings.reader_payoff: The address to Moses is heard as a contested dispatch whose grammatical movement conceals a social transfer of responsibility.
findings.containment: This is a phrase-level global contrast, not an identification of the scenes or agents and not a claim that the imperative loses its ordinary meaning of going.

findings.title: Combat is named and handed off
findings.claim: The dual imperative قَٰتِلَا names reciprocal combat as the action the speakers hand to the two addressees, while their own closing posture resonates with a wider pattern in which combat is requested or called for and then avoided.
findings.mechanism: The registered ق ت ل branch is öldürme amacıyla karşılıklı savaşma, carried by the focus Form III dual imperative. The exact 2:246 text records Bani Israil asking for combat and turning away when it is prescribed, while 3:167 records a pretext when people are called to fight; the focus combat command therefore meets an independent action-versus-withdrawal pattern.
findings.reader_payoff: The command to fight is no longer only a harsh instruction in the scene; it becomes the visible action from which the speakers' own non-participation is structurally separated.
findings.containment: The resonance does not claim a single historical event, identical motives, or that the focus dual imperative itself asserts that the speakers are cowardly; it preserves the ordinary combat sense.

epistemic.reason: The focus combat branch is registered and the target Arabic is exact, but the connections remain discovery nominations and provide no target morphology or lexical analysis.
